Hon'ble Shri Justice Ravindra Kumar Agrawal Order on Board 08.10.2024 1.

Present petition has been filed under Section 528 of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS 2023) against the order dated 29.06.2024 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Durg, District-Durg CG in Criminal Case-RCC/2128/2014, whereby the learned trial court has closed the rights of evidence of the petitioner with respect to prosecution witnesses PW1, PW2 and PW3 against the respondents for the offence Crmp 2741 of 2024 in crime No. 482/2012 registered at Police Station- Durg, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, and 34 of the IPC.
2.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class, Durg, District-Durg
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Brief facts relevant for adjudication of the case are that on 24.02.2021, petitioner has filed an application in Criminal Case No. RCC/2128/2014 for calling the original agreement dated Sunil Kumar Jain ( Lodha ) vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82914902/
1 21-10-2010 from the concerned Police Station which has been filed in the record of Civil Suit No.
46-A/2014, seized by the concerned Police in the offence, and sent for examination/report of handwriting expert.

entities.text: Sunil Kumar Jain ( Lodha ) vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since in the charge- sheet filed by the prosecution, it has been mentioned that the subject agreement has been sent for hand writing examination report before the State Examiner of Questioned Documents, Police Headquarter, Raipur, and as the report is awaited, application has been filed by the petitioner for calling the record of the Civil Suit and also calling the report from the State Examiner of Questioned Documents, Raipur, but the learned trial court has dismissed the said application on 26-11-2021.

3. The Criminal Revision No. 197/2021 filed by the petitioner has been allowed by the learned Sessions Judge, Durg vide order dated 10-02- 2022, directing the learned trial court to first investigate the matter in view of the reply of the Police Station Durg, with respect to the agreement dated 21-10-2010 filed in the said Civil Suit, and thereafter, to pass appropriate order on the application.

After passing of the order in Criminal Revision No. 197/2021 dated 10-02-2022, the learned trial court, without complying the said order, proceeded and without service of Crmp 2741 of 2024 bailable warrant upon the petitioner, the right of the evidence of the petitioner has been closed by order impugned dated 29.06.2024.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the trial court, without making compliance of the order dated 10.02.2022 passed in Cr. Revision No. 197/2021, proceeded in the case which is abuse of process of law, and vide impugned order dated 29-06-2024, closed the right of evidence of the petitioner.

He submits that the trial court ought to have looked into the agreement dated 21-10-2010 filed in Civil Suit No. 46-A/2014 and then passed order on the application of the petitioner, but in the present case, the learned trial court has not complied with the said order and has closed the right of evidence of the petitioner which is liable to be set aside.
He submits that if the evidence of the complainant is not recorded, then, advantage of the same will be in favour of the accused persons, and therefore, the impugned order is liable to be set aside.

5. Learned counsel for the State, on the contrary, opposing the petition, submits that in exercise of its powers under Section 482 of the CrPC, the Court would not embark on the enquiry to ascertain the veracity of the allegations.

According to learned counsel for the respondents, all those contentions which the Petitioner has raised, are in fact his defence and defence cannot be permitted to be a ground for quashing of the criminal prosecution itself in exercise of powers conferred upon this Court under Section 482 of the CrPC.

It is submitted that the High Court while exercising its powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C, Crmp 2741 of 2024 is neither exercising the appellate jurisdiction nor does it exercise the revisional jurisdiction and therefore, the powers so conferred upon this Court have to be used very sparingly, and not as a matter of routine.
6.

I have heard learned counsel for the parties and found that Criminal Revision No. 197/2021 filed by the petitioner was allowed by the learned Sessions Judge, Durg vide order dated 10.02.2022 directing the learned trial court to enquire about the matter, and thereafter to pass appropriate order.

On perusal of the record, it transpires that the agreement dated 21.10.2010 is not available on the record of the trial Court because the said document has been sent to to the Police Headquarters Raipur, for report of handwriting expert.
It has been mentioned that due to some technical fault, the accused persons will get the benefit and it will be an abuse of law against the petitioner.

It is clear that the original agreement dated 21.10.2010 was seized from the petitioner and it has been produced before the trial court, but the concerned signatures of the agreement have been sent for examination to the Police Headquarters, Raipur, and without receiving the report, the trial court had closed the rights of the petitioner.
Therefore, it is directed that the report of handwriting expert be first obtained and after compliance of the said order of the revisional court, the learned trial Court shall proceed further.

Thus, this Court finds that without complying with the revisional court's order dated 10-02-2022 in its true spirit, the learned trial court has closed the rights of the evidence of the petitioner therefore, the impugned order dated 29-06-2024 (Annexure P-1) passed by the learned trial court is Sunil Kumar Jain ( Lodha ) vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82914902/
3 set aside, and it is directed that the agreement be first obtained and after complying with the order of revisional court passed on 10.02.2022, the learned trial court shall proceed further, for recording evidence of PW1, PW2, PW3, and other witnesses.
10. Learned trial Court is directed to make all its endeavour to call for the agreement dated 21.10.2010, and then proceed with the matter expeditiously.
11.
